scope: Foundational mechanisms and fixed-paper results. These are separate benchmark experiments, not a cross-paper leaderboard or utility-deployment reliability evidence.

papers.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
papers.mechanism: Interleave proposed reasoning steps with environment actions and returned observations in the prompt history. Domain actions obtain new evidence; generated text can update a plan but does not itself change the environment.
executable_workflow: Provide a task, permitted action grammar and few-shot demonstration trajectories.
Generate a next action from task and recorded observations; reject malformed or out-of-scope actions in the application.
Execute the selected environment action and append its observation to the context.
Repeat until finish or a fixed budget is reached. Stopping and software gates are explicit tutorial implementation requirements.

result.metric: Success rate (%) = fraction of episodes satisfying all requested product requirements
result.count_note: Do not reverse-engineer integer successes from rounded rates; the paper states the task-set size but does not provide raw per-method counts here.

supporting_results.limitation: The 71% headline selects the best of six prompt settings; do not describe it as the average result.
ReAct does not improve every task/model/metric. These are separate experiments from the WebShop chart.

papers.implementation_distinction: ReAct is a 2022/2023 prompting and interaction paradigm, not an orchestration SDK. The original repository supplies GPT-3 notebooks; that code/backend differs from the PaLM-540B main-paper result. Later LangGraph/other implementations are separate software products.
limitations: The benchmark is a simulated shopping environment, not a utility-control deployment.
Observations may be unhelpful or wrong; generated reasoning can repeat or misinterpret them.
No engineering feasibility, permission or operating-time guarantee follows from this benchmark.
Few-shot examples and model/backend choice materially affect results.
papers.utility_transfer: Illustrative transfer only: a bounded advisory agent may resolve an asset, retrieve a versioned measurement, call an offline simulator and return evidence. Each tool still needs typed parameters, version checks, constraints and authorization.

papers.title: Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools
papers.code_status: No official Toolformer implementation was identified in the checked paper, publisher or Meta publication page. Do not attribute third-party reimplementations to the paper authors.
papers.mechanism: Generate candidate API annotations on a language-model corpus, execute the calls, keep only calls whose responses improve prediction of subsequent text, and fine-tune the language model on retained call-and-result examples.
papers.filter_formula: Keep a call if L_i^- - L_i^+ >= tau_f, where L_i^- is min(loss without call, loss with call but without response) and L_i^+ includes the response.
executable_workflow: Offline: sample candidate calls at candidate positions in existing texts.
Execute candidate APIs, then score the original continuation with and without each response.
Filter by the stated loss-improvement threshold and fine-tune on retained augmented texts.
At inference: pause generation on the API delimiter, execute the call, insert the returned result and continue.

result.model: Same fine-tuned GPT-J Toolformer model in both chart arms
result.denominator_note: Evaluated MAWPS sample count is not disclosed in this paper's reported setup; do not substitute an external dataset's nominal size.
result.evaluation_detail: First generated number is scored, except that if an equation is produced the first number after '=' is scored. This is a more lenient criterion than exact-string match.
result.inference_budget: At most one API call per input; API-start token considered among top10 candidates rather than ordinary greedy-only top1.

papers.implementation_distinction: This paper changes model weights through self-supervised fine-tuning. Adding a function schema to a current SDK prompt does not reproduce Toolformer training. The runtime interrupt/call/resume pattern is one component of the method.
limitations: Only one API call per evaluation input; original training does not teach chained tool calls or interactive search refinement.
Lower next-token loss is a training utility criterion, not a proof of engineering correctness or safe action.
The paper's calculator supports four arithmetic operations and rounds to two decimal places; that tool is not a power-system solver.
Call selection is sensitive to wording and does not account for tool-dependent computational cost.
papers.utility_transfer: Illustrative lesson: decide which operations should be delegated to deterministic domain tools and evaluate whether the selected call adds useful evidence. Do not use a generic calculator's improvement to infer AC power-flow competence.

papers.title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
papers.authorship_note: The NeurIPS published paper lists five authors. The repository/arXiv citation also includes Edward Berman; do not silently combine version-specific author lists.
papers.mechanism: An actor attempts a task; an evaluator supplies feedback; a reflection model converts the failure and trajectory into text retained in episodic memory for the next attempt. The language-model weights stay fixed.
executable_workflow: Generate a candidate program and a small internal test suite.
Run tests/compiler and retain concrete failure information.
Generate a concise reflection and condition the next attempt on that feedback and retained memory.

Stop on the internal success gate or a prespecified trial budget; evaluate the final selected program separately on benchmark tests. In a utility adaptation, the independent engineering checker is an additional requirement.

result.dataset: 50 hardest HumanEval problems translated to Rust using MultiPL-E
result.metric: Reported pass@1 accuracy (%) of final procedure output
result.budget_note: The procedure can revise internally before returning its selected output. Pass@1 is not one model call and the chart is not an equal-compute comparison.
result.count_note: Percentages and sample-set size are reproduced; no raw success counts are reconstructed.

supporting_results.limitation: Headline is after an internal test/reflection procedure. Exact Python sample denominator is not stated beside this table; use the50-task Rust ablation for an explicit-n chart.
The method is not uniformly improving; self-generated tests can accept a wrong implementation.

papers.implementation_distinction: Reflexion is an inference-time feedback/memory architecture. It does not update neural weights, and it is not a current hosted SDK or an automatic guarantee that self-evaluation is correct.
limitations: Incorrect self-generated tests can cause false acceptance or harmful repair of correct code.
The no-test ablation falls below the baseline; ungrounded self-critique can worsen the result.
The paper reports failure to improve meaningfully on a100-environment WebShop experiment after four trials (AppendixB.1, PDFp.14).
Results use coding/QA/games, not utility operating actions; costs and repeated attempts must be counted.
papers.utility_transfer: Illustrative transfer only: retain a failed simulator/checker report and a concise repair note for another offline candidate. Preserve checker results independently from the model's explanation; never turn a remembered suggestion into an operating rule automatically.

papers.title: Language Agent Tree Search Unifies Reasoning, Acting, and Planning in Language Models
papers.mechanism: Online trajectory search. States contain task, action history and observations. UCT selects; the LM samples actions; environment feedback plus LM/self-consistency scoring evaluates children. Simulate, backpropagate reward, and retain failed trajectories with reflections as future context. Stop on success or budget. No weight training or learned world model.

result.recommended_chart: WebShop score among prompting methods; success rate is a separate metric.
result.locator: Table 6 and Section 5.3, p.8; Appendix D.3, pp.16–17
result.comparison_note: LATS, ReAct best-of-k and Reflexion share k=30, not equal model-call/token budgets. Other Table 6 training/human rows are not controlled same-model comparisons.

papers.limits: Higher inference cost than simpler prompting; requires reverting environments to earlier states. Benchmarks simplify real-world interaction.

papers.teaching_inference: For a utility operator, branch and replay in a simulator or reversible workspace. Search over draft actions; commit real-world changes only after selecting an outcome. The paper does not establish safe rollback of irreversible external actions.

papers.title: AFlow: Automating Agentic Workflow Generation
papers.mechanism: Offline search over complete executable workflows. MCTS tree nodes are whole workflows; an optimizer edits prompts and code connections. Model, temperature and output format stay fixed. Reusable operators narrow the search. Mixed uniform/score selection, repeated execution evaluation, and parent-linked experience guide subsequent edits.
papers.discovered_workflow: MBPP: generate three programs; ensemble-select; test; return on success, otherwise repair using failure feedback.

result.recommended_chart: MBPP only; avoid averaging incompatible benchmark metrics.
result.denominator_note: Exact MBPP test count undisclosed in paper. Full dataset split 20% validation/80% test, seed 42; do not substitute the standard MBPP test size.

papers.limits: Requires numerical evaluation; validation-driven workflow discovery has search cost. Results concern benchmark workflows. Different executors may need different workflows.

repository_workflow.status: Source-inspected, not executed; commands require credentials and historical model availability.
steps: Configure models and credentials in config/config2.yaml using the example.

repository_workflow.source_notes: Current run.py automatically downloads datasets. Its validation_rounds default is 1, unlike the paper's 5: pass 5 explicitly. README warns some operators may have migration bugs. Current code defaults do not establish exact paper reproduction.

papers.teaching_inference: Treat this as outer-loop process improvement: first define a reliable score, then compare candidate procedures on held-out examples. AFlow's optimized workflow is the deployed artifact; the search tree is not the user's live task state.

papers.implementation_distinction: AFlow is a research workflow-optimization framework. Its MCTS nodes are whole workflows, unlike task-trajectory nodes in LATS. A general orchestration SDK does not automatically perform this offline optimization or supply the evaluation score.

Label published figures as original source figures; new plots reproduce reported values, while deltas are tutorial calculations.

Additional failure analyses and original paper figures

mechanism_synthesis: AFlow searches for the procedure used across tasks; LATS searches alternative paths within a task. An orchestration SDK can implement either control structure but does not automatically supply its evaluator, budget, reversible environment or evidence of improvement.
